a: A family chore game. Everyone in the family earns points for the chores they do, a live scoreboard shows who's ahead, and whoever has the most points on Sunday night wins the week. Points can be spent on rewards the parents choose.

q: Do kids need their own phone?
a: No. Parents add kids as profiles, and Kid Mode lets a child tick off their own chores on a parent's phone. Older kids can join on their own phone with the family code a parent shares.
If you want. By default everyone competes, so a parent can lose to an eight-year-old. You can switch to kids-only, where parents coach and their points still count toward the family goal.

When a kid finishes a task it waits for a parent's OK before the points land. Parents get one notification, approve everything from one inbox, or send a task back with a quick note. Small tasks can be approved automatically.

q: What keeps it fun after the first few weeks?
a: A new weekly twist (like double points for chores), streaks with a streak shield, levels with real-world perks you choose, bounties, a comeback boost for whoever finished last, 4-week seasons, and stickers parents send just to say well done.

Optionally. Parents set a rate and kids can ask to cash out; a parent approves it and pays outside the app. Chore League never holds or moves money, and bonus points from weekly twists stay in the game.

q: Can we play against other families?
a: Yes. Start a family league and share its code with up to five other families. Families are compared on average points per player, so a small family can beat a big one. Other families only ever see your family's league name and score.

q: Which phones does it work on?
a: Android today, with iPhone coming next.
